newsitem.title: USA: CFTC sets June 12 meeting on CBOT delivery dispute.
newsitem.headline: CFTC sets June 12 meeting on CBOT delivery dispute.

text.p: A public meeting will be held June 12 on the Chicago Board of Trade's controversial proposal to change delivery terms of its corn and soybean futures contracts, the Commodity Futures Trading Commission said Thursday.
The agency said it set aside three hours for what is an unusual public hearing on a pending CFTC issue.
Some 300 comments have been submitted by farm groups, midwestern politicians and elevators, virtually all opposing the CBOT plan to elminate Toledo as a delivery point.

Under pressure by the CFTC to make changes reflecting the scarcity of warehouse space in Chicago, the CBOT proposed designating the northern Illinois River as a central site for traders to take physical delivery of soybeans and corn contracts.
Supporters of the port of Toledo have complained that the CBOT proposal would ignore the needs of southeastern grain buyers, and could contribute to market manipulation.
